persons.name: Julia
persons.harm: Recruited as a teenager into a charismatic church (described as a cult) where the youth pastor and senior pastor controlled her dating, extracted years of unpaid or underpaid labour, accused her of premarital sex, and publicly 'exposed' her pregnancy before the congregation, after which she was made to step down from her roles; wages were withheld for weeks during the church's financial collapse.
persons.perpetrator_role: the church's youth pastor (later senior pastor, show pseudonym withheld) and his father, the senior pastor

quotes.quote: they believed that the church leadership and the youth leadership should have a say and be able to speak into your lives as authority figures and people that you would check in with
he did an episode where he had a specialist who talked about cults and that's that was kind of my like oh crap moment where I realized you were in a cult.
I think I thought that I was handling it and that it was fine and it was something I could manage on my own. So I didn't really talk to them about that part.

persons.outcome_quote: Is the church still active and alive and is he still a pastor? It's still active and alive, he is still a pastor.
persons.notes: The abuser was the church itself (its youth pastor and senior pastor); no outside institution was ever told. The public 'exposing our sin' before the congregation and being made to step down were acts of the abusing institution and are coded as the harm, not as a response, so harmed_by_institution_ever is false and there are no contacts. Julia left the church on her own (around her third pregnancy) about seven years before the interview. Her parents later said 'they couldn't do anything to stop it' (s5-e1 @ 23:40). Second witness: host Tiffany attended the same church and confirms parts (e.g. 'I can confirm that story' re the overweight member, s5-e1 @ 33:01); Kelly (s5-e3) corroborates the church's child labour. Reason 'other' = she thought she could handle it herself.

persons.name: Kelly
persons.harm: Married at about 21 to the church's youth pastor (the senior pastor's adopted son), who isolated her from family and friends, controlled her clothing and contacts, threatened divorce if she raised concerns, diverted her wages into his own paycheck, repeatedly forced sex on her, and struck her and called her names during their last sexual encounter after separation.
persons.perpetrator_role: her ex-husband (unlicensed marriage), the church's youth pastor and adopted son of the senior pastor

quotes.quote: He started telling me that if I were to mention my discomfort at the time and proximity to this girl, he would divorce me immediately.
One of the secrets that I was told to keep was that we had sex before we got married. And I was told that revealing this truth would damage his reputation to the point of no return.
I didn't begin to classify it as rape until after we were separated.

all of the counselors that I had seen previously wore people from our life that he had directed me to, and also told me, you know, get help for your problems, but don't you dare say a bad word about me.
Oh, I was absolutely alone. My husband had strategically cut out all of the women influences in my life.

contacts.institution: licensed male marriage counselor chosen by her husband; attended and tithed to the church, paid by the church for her sessions

contacts.what_was_asked: Help in the separation; she disclosed that she was not appreciated during sex and described rape, and the financial control was visible in sessions.
contacts.what_institution_did: Minimized her account and her earlier therapy trauma, refused to refer her elsewhere despite the conflict of interest, framed the sexual abuse as her husband not pleasuring her well enough, blamed the breakdown on their lack of a marriage license, and never told her she could go to police.
contacts.quote: His response to me was that my husband wasn't doing his job to pleasure me and he needed to do better. Not that I had been victimized or that what he did was wrong and hurtful, but just that he wasn't doing his job well enough.
contacts.what_happened_next: Counseling continued; the counselor then pressed her toward a financial agreement benefiting the husband.
contacts.notes: Could also be read as protected_itself (counselor financially tied to the church) or blaming her ('you're outside of God's will', s5-e5 @ 22:14). Earlier he 'minimized my response' when she raised his conflict of interest (s5-e5 @ 17:07).

contacts.what_institution_did: Breached confidentiality by telling the senior pastor (her father-in-law and boss) what she had said; the pastor then discussed her sessions with her mother.

contacts.what_happened_next: The senior pastor learned what she said in therapy and passed it on to her mother (s5-e6 @ 8:11).

The couple also saw the senior pastor as couples counselor briefly ('[perpetrator] did not say that', s5-e5 @ 18:07), but she says she never told him of the sexual/emotional abuse, so not coded. Police never contacted. Her family (stepdad, parents) believed and supported her. Wages: W2 for $29 from the senior pastor's restaurant; she never investigated.

persons.harm: Dated the same youth pastor from about 18; he controlled her dress and whom she saw, forbade her from seeing her friend group, and after the breakup spread lies that she had cheated on him.

coder_notes: Season 5 'survivor short stories': Julia (e1-2) and Kelly (e3-6) about the same charismatic church in the Sacramento area (the youth/senior pastor's show pseudonym is withheld and replaced by [perpetrator] in quotes); Rachel (e7-14) about abusive evangelical pastor parents in Scotland/Hawaii; e15 is an expert interview on political gaslighting with no individual case. All 8 chunk files read in full. No unassigned episode opened (none relevant by title/description). Judgment calls: Julia coded never_reached because the abuser was the church itself; Rachel's mother included as a DV victim although she is also a perpetrator against the children (flagged, low confidence); Catherine included with low confidence; decisive work for Daniel/Sarah coded family_or_friends (reports by a family friend after Rachel's discovery, plus sibling disclosure) where 'institution' is arguable. Rachel's father's trial was pending at the season's end.
